en: I am standing in the queue at the bank.
tamil: நான் வங்கியில வரிசையில நிக்கிறேன்.
context: Telling a friend where you are on the phone.
explain: Present continuous with 'am' shows an action happening right now.
usage: Use it on a phone call when someone asks where you are.
leelaQ: Do you like going to the bank, or do you prefer online banking?
answer: I prefer online banking because it saves a lot of time.

en: Can I open a savings account here today?
tamil: நான் இன்னைக்கு இங்க சேமிப்பு கணக்கு தொடங்கலாமா?
context: Asking a bank clerk about a new account.
explain: 'Can I ...?' is a simple way to ask for permission or possibility.
usage: Say this to the bank staff at the help desk when you want a new account.
leelaQ: Do you have a savings account? Which bank is it in?
answer: Yes, I have a savings account in a government bank.

en: I paid the electricity bill online yesterday.
tamil: நேத்து மின்சார கட்டணத்தை ஆன்லைன்ல கட்டிட்டேன்.
context: Telling your father the bill is already paid.
explain: 'Paid' is the past form of 'pay'. 'Yesterday' tells us when it happened.
usage: Use it at home when family asks whether a bill is paid.
leelaQ: How do you pay your electricity bill every month?
answer: I pay it online using my phone.

en: Could you please check my balance?
tamil: என் இருப்பை கொஞ்சம் பார்த்து சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a bank employee for help.
explain: 'Could you please ...?' is a very polite way to request something.
usage: Use it politely with a bank clerk or at an ATM kiosk helper.
leelaQ: How often do you check your bank balance?
answer: I check my balance once a week.

en: I do not have change for five hundred rupees.
tamil: என்கிட்ட ஐநூறு ரூபாய்க்கு சில்லறை இல்ல.
context: Telling an auto driver you have no small notes.
explain: 'Change' here means small notes and coins. 'Do not have' shows you lack something.
usage: Say it to a driver or shopkeeper when you only have a big note.
leelaQ: What do you do when a shop has no change for you?
answer: I pay by UPI instead of using cash.

en: I will transfer the money to your account tonight.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி உங்க கணக்குக்கு பணம் அனுப்பறேன்.
context: Promising a friend to send money.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise or decision made for the future.
usage: Use it with a friend or relative who is waiting for money.
leelaQ: Have you ever sent money to a friend? How did you do it?
answer: Yes, I sent money to my friend using a mobile app.

en: Which UPI app do you use for payments?
tamil: நீங்க பணம் கட்ட எந்த UPI ஆப் பயன்படுத்தறீங்க?
context: Chatting with a colleague about phone payments.
explain: 'Which' is used when we choose from a few known options.
usage: Ask it casually with friends or colleagues when talking about apps.
leelaQ: What do you usually pay for using your phone?
answer: I pay for groceries and auto fares using my phone.

en: I have saved ten thousand rupees this year.
tamil: இந்த வருஷம் பத்தாயிரம் ரூபாய் சேமிச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Proudly telling a friend about your savings.
explain: Present perfect 'have saved' links a past action to the present result.
usage: Use it when you talk about your savings goals with friends or family.
leelaQ: How much do you want to save this year?
answer: I want to save twenty thousand rupees this year.

en: Please scan this QR code to pay.
tamil: பணம் கட்ட இந்த QR கோடை ஸ்கேன் பண்ணுங்க.
context: A shopkeeper asking a customer to pay by phone.
explain: 'Please' makes an order sound polite. 'To pay' tells the purpose.
usage: A shop owner says this at the counter when a customer wants to pay by UPI.
leelaQ: Do you pay by QR code in small shops?
answer: Yes, most small shops near my house accept QR codes.

en: You should keep your ATM PIN secret.
tamil: உங்க ATM பின்னை ரகசியமா வச்சுக்கணும்.
context: Advising an elderly relative about card safety.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. 'Keep ... secret' means do not tell anyone.
usage: Use it when you advise family members about safe banking.
leelaQ: How do you keep your bank details safe?
answer: I never tell my PIN to anyone.

en: Did the payment go through on your phone?
tamil: உங்க போன்ல பணம் போயிடுச்சா?
context: Asking a friend after a UPI payment.
explain: 'Go through' means a payment or request was successful.
usage: Ask it right after someone pays in a shop or on a call.
leelaQ: Has a payment ever failed for you? What did you do?
answer: Yes, once it failed, so I tried again after some time.

en: My salary comes into my account on the first of every month.
tamil: என் சம்பளம் மாசம் ஒண்ணாம் தேதி என் கணக்குல வரும்.
context: Telling a friend when you get paid.
explain: Simple present is used for regular habits and fixed schedules.
usage: Use it when you talk about your monthly money plan.
leelaQ: When do you get your salary or pocket money?
answer: I get my pocket money on the first of every month.

en: The card payment did not work at the shop.
tamil: கடையில கார்டு பேமெண்ட் வேலை செய்யல.
context: Explaining a payment problem to a friend.
explain: 'Did not work' is the negative past. The verb 'work' stays in base form.
usage: Use it to explain why you had to pay in cash or try another way.
leelaQ: What do you do if your card does not work?
answer: I pay with cash or use my phone.

en: I am making a budget for the next month.
tamil: அடுத்த மாசத்துக்கு ஒரு பட்ஜெட் போடறேன்.
context: Telling your spouse about monthly planning.
explain: Present continuous shows work in progress. 'Make a budget' is a common phrase.
usage: Use it at home when you plan monthly spending with your family.
leelaQ: What are the main things in your monthly budget?
answer: Rent, food and travel are the main things in my budget.

en: When will the loan be approved?
tamil: லோன் எப்போ சாங்ஷன் ஆகும்?
context: Asking a bank officer about your loan.
explain: 'Will be approved' is a passive future form. It focuses on the loan, not the person.
usage: Ask it at the bank when you are waiting for a loan decision.
leelaQ: What would you take a loan for, if you needed one?
answer: I would take a loan to buy a house.

en: Can you give me a receipt for this payment?
tamil: இந்த பணத்துக்கு ஒரு ரசீது தர முடியுமா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper for proof of payment.
explain: 'Can you give me ...?' is a simple polite request.
usage: Say it at a shop, school office or clinic after you pay.
leelaQ: Why is it good to keep a receipt?
answer: It is good because I can show it if there is a problem.

en: I forgot my debit card at home today.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு என் டெபிட் கார்டை வீட்டுலயே மறந்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend why you cannot pay by card.
explain: 'Forgot' is the past of 'forget'. 'At home' tells where the card is.
usage: Use it with friends or colleagues when you cannot pay.
leelaQ: What do you do when you forget your wallet at home?
answer: I use my phone to pay.

en: I am going to pay the loan instalment on Friday.
tamil: வெள்ளிக்கிழமை லோன் தவணை கட்டப் போறேன்.
context: Telling someone your plan for a loan payment.
explain: 'Am going to' talks about a plan you have already made.
usage: Use it with a bank officer or family when you speak of a payment plan.
leelaQ: What payments do you have to make every month?
answer: I have to pay rent and a phone bill every month.

en: How much is the interest on this loan?
tamil: இந்த லோனுக்கு வட்டி எவ்வளவு?
context: Asking a loan officer about the cost.
explain: 'How much' asks for an amount. Interest is the extra money you pay on a loan.
usage: Ask it before you take a loan from a bank or a finance office.
leelaQ: Why should we ask about interest before taking a loan?
answer: Because interest decides how much extra money we must pay.

en: The bank closes at four in the afternoon.
tamil: வங்கி மதியம் நாலு மணிக்கு மூடிடுவாங்க.
context: Warning a friend about bank timing.
explain: Simple present is used for fixed timings.
usage: Use it to tell someone to hurry before the bank shuts.
leelaQ: What time do shops near your house close?
answer: They close at nine at night.

en: You must not share your OTP with anyone.
tamil: உங்க OTP-ஐ யார்கிட்டயும் சொல்லக்கூடாது.
context: Warning a parent about fraud calls.
explain: 'Must not' is a strong rule. It shows something is forbidden or dangerous.
usage: Say it to family or friends to protect them from phone fraud.
leelaQ: What should we do if a stranger asks for our OTP?
answer: We should cut the call and tell the bank.

en: Please fill this form and sign here.
tamil: இந்த படிவத்தை நிரப்பி இங்க கையெழுத்து போடுங்க.
context: A bank clerk giving instructions to a customer.
explain: Two actions joined by 'and'. 'Please' keeps the tone polite.
usage: Bank and office staff use this when a customer must complete a form.
leelaQ: Do you find forms easy or difficult to fill?
answer: I find them a little difficult because they are long.

en: The money has reached my account.
tamil: பணம் என் கணக்குக்கு வந்துடுச்சு.
context: Telling a friend the payment arrived.
explain: 'Has reached' shows the money came and is there now.
usage: Use it after a friend or customer says they sent money.
leelaQ: How do you know when money comes into your account?
answer: I get an SMS from the bank.

en: Should I take a loan for a new bike?
tamil: புது பைக்குக்கு லோன் எடுக்கலாமா?
context: Asking a friend for advice on buying a bike.
explain: 'Should I ...?' asks for advice or an opinion.
usage: Ask it with an elder, a friend or a bank agent before a big purchase.
leelaQ: Would you buy a bike with a loan or with savings?
answer: I would buy it with savings because loans cost more.

en: We spent too much on groceries last month.
tamil: போன மாசம் மளிகைக்கு ரொம்ப செலவு பண்ணிட்டோம்.
context: Talking with your wife about household expenses.
explain: 'Too much' means more than needed. 'Spent' is the past of 'spend'.
usage: Use it when you review the family budget at home.
leelaQ: How can a family spend less on groceries?
answer: We can make a list and buy only what we need.

en: Petrol prices go up almost every month.
tamil: பெட்ரோல் விலை கிட்டத்தட்ட ஒவ்வொரு மாசமும் ஏறுது.
context: Complaining about fuel cost with a colleague.
explain: Simple present with 'almost every month' shows a regular pattern.
usage: Use it in casual talk when people discuss rising costs.
leelaQ: How do rising petrol prices affect your life?
answer: I now use public transport more often.

en: Is there any charge for withdrawing cash?
tamil: பணம் எடுக்க ஏதாவது கட்டணம் இருக்கா?
context: Asking at the bank about ATM fees.
explain: 'Is there any ...?' checks whether something exists.
usage: Ask it at the bank or ATM counter before taking out money.
leelaQ: Do you carry cash or do you mostly use your phone?
answer: I carry a little cash and use my phone for the rest.

en: I am waiting for the SMS from the bank.
tamil: வங்கியில இருந்து SMS-காக காத்துட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling someone why you cannot finish a payment.
explain: 'Am waiting for' shows you are in the middle of waiting.
usage: Use it when an OTP or confirmation has not come yet.
leelaQ: What do you do when an OTP does not arrive?
answer: I wait for one minute and then ask for it again.

en: Could you help me fill this deposit slip?
tamil: இந்த டெபாசிட் சீட்டை நிரப்ப உதவ முடியுமா?
context: Asking a bank staff member for help.
explain: 'Could you help me ...?' is polite when you need support.
usage: Use it with bank staff or a helpful person when a form is confusing.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you do not understand a form?
answer: My brother helps me with forms.

en: I will pay you back by next Monday.
tamil: அடுத்த திங்கள்கிழமைக்குள்ள உங்களுக்கு திருப்பி கொடுத்துடறேன்.
context: Promising a friend to return borrowed money.
explain: 'Pay back' means return money. 'By' gives a deadline.
usage: Say it when you borrow a small amount from a friend or relative.
leelaQ: Is it a good idea to borrow money from friends?
answer: It is fine for small amounts if we pay back on time.

en: I never lend money to strangers.
tamil: தெரியாதவங்களுக்கு நான் ஒருநாளும் பணம் கடன் கொடுக்கமாட்டேன்.
context: Explaining your rule about money.
explain: 'Never' makes the sentence negative. It is used with habits.
usage: Use it to politely refuse when an unknown person asks for money.
leelaQ: Would you lend money to a close friend?
answer: Yes, I would lend a small amount to a close friend.

en: I got a message about a failed transaction.
tamil: தோல்வியடைந்த பரிவர்த்தனை பத்தி ஒரு மெசேஜ் வந்தது.
context: Telling the bank about a payment problem.
explain: 'Got a message' is a common spoken way to say 'received a message'.
usage: Use it on a bank helpline call when money is cut but not received.
leelaQ: What will you do if money is cut but the payment fails?
answer: I will call the bank and give the transaction details.

en: Have you paid the house rent this month?
tamil: இந்த மாசம் வீட்டு வாடகை கட்டிட்டீங்களா?
context: Asking your flatmate about rent.
explain: 'Have you ...?' asks whether something is done by now.
usage: Ask it to a flatmate or family member who handles the rent.
leelaQ: Who pays the rent in your home?
answer: My father pays the rent every month.

en: Gold rate is high these days.
tamil: இப்போ தங்கம் விலை ரொம்ப அதிகமா இருக்கு.
context: Chatting with relatives before a wedding.
explain: 'These days' means at the present time.
usage: Use it in family talk about jewellery or weddings.
leelaQ: Do people in your family buy gold for weddings?
answer: Yes, we always buy some gold for weddings.

en: Tell me the exact amount before you swipe the card.
tamil: கார்டை தேய்க்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி சரியான தொகையை சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a cashier to confirm the bill.
explain: 'Before' connects two actions in order. 'Exact' means correct, not roughly.
usage: Say it at a shop counter so you can check the total.
leelaQ: Why should we check the amount before we pay?
answer: So we do not pay a wrong amount by mistake.

en: We can save more if we cook at home.
tamil: வீட்டுல சமைச்சா நிறைய சேமிக்கலாம்.
context: Talking about reducing food expenses.
explain: 'If' sentences show a condition and its result.
usage: Use it when you discuss ways to spend less with family.
leelaQ: What is one habit that helps you save money?
answer: I carry lunch from home to save money.

en: Do you accept Google Pay here?
tamil: இங்க Google Pay வாங்கிப்பீங்களா?
context: Asking a shopkeeper before buying.
explain: 'Do you accept ...?' asks which payment ways a shop allows.
usage: Ask it at a small shop or restaurant before you order.
leelaQ: Which payment method do you use the most?
answer: I use UPI the most.

en: My card has expired, so I need a new one.
tamil: என் கார்டு காலாவதி ஆகிடுச்சு, அதனால புது கார்டு வேணும்.
context: Talking to bank staff about a card problem.
explain: 'So' connects a reason with a result.
usage: Use it at the bank counter or on a helpline when you need a replacement.
leelaQ: What do you do when your bank card stops working?
answer: I visit the bank and ask for a new card.

en: I did not receive the refund yet.
tamil: ரீஃபண்ட் இன்னும் எனக்கு வரல.
context: Calling customer care about a refund.
explain: 'Did not receive' is the negative past. 'Yet' shows you still expect it.
usage: Say it to customer care when an online order refund is late.
leelaQ: How long do you wait for a refund before you complain?
answer: I wait for about a week and then I call them.

en: The shopkeeper gave me ten rupees extra change by mistake.
tamil: கடைக்காரர் தவறுதலா எனக்கு பத்து ரூபாய் அதிகமா சில்லறை கொடுத்துட்டார்.
context: Telling a friend about an honest moment.
explain: 'By mistake' means not on purpose.
usage: Use it when you tell a story about money and honesty.
leelaQ: What would you do if a shopkeeper gave you extra change?
answer: I would return the extra money to him.

en: Could I pay half now and half later?
tamil: பாதி இப்போ, பாதி அப்புறம் கட்டலாமா?
context: Asking a shop owner for a payment option.
explain: 'Could I ...?' is a polite way to ask for something unusual.
usage: Ask it when you need to split a payment with a shop or a school office.
leelaQ: Do you like to pay in parts or all at once?
answer: I like to pay all at once, so I am free of tension.

en: Prices will come down after the festival season.
tamil: பண்டிகை சீசன் முடிஞ்சதும் விலை குறையும்.
context: Advising a friend to wait before buying.
explain: 'Will' is used for a prediction. 'Come down' means become lower.
usage: Use it when you tell someone to wait for a better price.
leelaQ: When do you usually shop for clothes or gadgets?
answer: I shop during big festival sales.

en: He is checking the bill line by line.
tamil: அவர் பில்லை ஒவ்வொரு வரியா சரிபார்க்கிறார்.
context: Describing a careful person at a restaurant.
explain: 'Line by line' means slowly, one line at a time.
usage: Use it when you describe someone who is very careful with money.
leelaQ: Do you check your bill carefully at restaurants?
answer: Yes, I always check it before I pay.

en: Would you mind splitting the bill with me?
tamil: பில்லை என்கூட பிரிச்சுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend to share the cost.
explain: 'Would you mind ...ing?' is a gentle and polite request.
usage: Use it after a meal when friends share the cost.
leelaQ: Do you share bills with friends when you eat out?
answer: Yes, we split the bill equally.

en: I opened a recurring deposit last week.
tamil: போன வாரம் ஒரு ஆர்.டி. கணக்கு தொடங்கினேன்.
context: Telling a colleague about a savings plan.
explain: 'Opened' is the past of 'open'. A recurring deposit means saving a fixed amount monthly.
usage: Use it when you talk about savings plans with colleagues.
leelaQ: What is a good way to save a little money every month?
answer: A recurring deposit is a good way to save every month.

en: What is the minimum balance in this account?
tamil: இந்த கணக்குல குறைந்தபட்ச இருப்பு எவ்வளவு?
context: Asking the bank before opening an account.
explain: 'Minimum balance' is the least money you must keep in the account.
usage: Ask it at the bank before you open any new account.
leelaQ: Why is it important to know the minimum balance?
answer: Because the bank can charge a fee if we go below it.

en: I keep a small emergency fund for sudden expenses.
tamil: திடீர் செலவுகளுக்கு கொஞ்சம் அவசர நிதி வச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Explaining your saving habit.
explain: 'Keep' is used for money you set aside. 'Sudden' means unexpected.
usage: Use it when you talk about safe money habits with friends.
leelaQ: What kind of sudden expenses can happen in a family?
answer: A medical bill or a repair can happen suddenly.

en: You cannot withdraw more than ten thousand rupees from this ATM.
tamil: இந்த ATM-ல பத்தாயிரத்துக்கு மேல எடுக்க முடியாது.
context: Explaining the daily limit to a friend.
explain: 'Cannot' shows a limit or rule. 'More than' compares amounts.
usage: Use it to warn someone about an ATM limit.
leelaQ: How much cash do you usually take out at one time?
answer: I take out about two thousand rupees at one time.

en: The EMI is deducted from my account on the fifth.
tamil: EMI ஐந்தாம் தேதி என் கணக்குல இருந்து பிடிச்சுக்குவாங்க.
context: Explaining a monthly loan payment.
explain: Passive 'is deducted' focuses on what happens to the money.
usage: Use it when you tell someone why you need money in the account by a date.
leelaQ: Which date of the month is hardest for you money-wise?
answer: The end of the month is hardest because my money is finished.

en: I'm going to start a small SIP next month.
tamil: அடுத்த மாசம் ஒரு சின்ன SIP தொடங்கப் போறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about investing.
explain: 'I'm going to' shows a plan. A SIP is a monthly investment.
usage: Use it when you talk about your investment plan with friends.
leelaQ: What would you like to invest in some day?
answer: I would like to invest in mutual funds.

en: Why was my payment declined?
tamil: என் பேமெண்ட் ஏன் நிராகரிக்கப்பட்டது?
context: Calling bank customer care.
explain: 'Why' asks the reason. 'Declined' means the payment was refused.
usage: Ask it on a helpline call when your payment fails.
leelaQ: What can be the reasons for a declined payment?
answer: The balance may be low or the network may be weak.

en: My phone recharge is due tomorrow.
tamil: என் போன் ரீசார்ஜ் நாளைக்கு முடியுது.
context: Telling a friend about a plan expiry.
explain: 'Due' means something must be paid or done by a time.
usage: Use it when you remind yourself or others about a payment date.
leelaQ: How often do you recharge your phone?
answer: I recharge it once a month.

en: Keep the receipt safe in case you need a refund.
tamil: பணம் திருப்பி வேணும்னா தேவைப்படும், ரசீதை பத்திரமா வச்சுக்கோங்க.
context: Advising a friend after buying something.
explain: 'In case' means because something may happen later.
usage: Use it when you advise a friend after a purchase.
leelaQ: Where do you keep important bills and receipts?
answer: I keep them in a file at home.

en: I checked three shops before buying this phone.
tamil: இந்த போனை வாங்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி மூணு கடை பார்த்தேன்.
context: Telling a friend how you compared prices.
explain: 'Before buying' uses the -ing form after 'before'.
usage: Use it when you tell a friend how you found a good deal.
leelaQ: How do you find the best price for something?
answer: I compare prices in a few shops and on the internet.

en: This shop does not take credit cards.
tamil: இந்த கடையில கிரெடிட் கார்டு எடுத்துக்க மாட்டாங்க.
context: Telling a friend about a payment rule.
explain: 'Does not take' says what the shop refuses to accept.
usage: Use it to warn a friend before they shop and find no card option.
leelaQ: Do you prefer credit cards or debit cards?
answer: I prefer debit cards because I cannot overspend.

en: Can I get a printout of my bank statement?
tamil: என் வங்கி அறிக்கையை பிரிண்ட் எடுத்து தர முடியுமா?
context: Asking at the bank counter.
explain: 'Can I get ...?' is a common way to ask for a service.
usage: Ask it at the bank when you need a statement for a visa or loan.
leelaQ: When do people need a bank statement?
answer: They need it for a loan or a visa.

en: Everything is getting costlier these days.
tamil: இப்பல்லாம் எல்லாமே விலை ஏறிட்டே போகுது.
context: Complaining about prices to a neighbour.
explain: 'Getting costlier' shows a change that keeps happening.
usage: Use it in everyday talk about rising prices.
leelaQ: What has become costlier in your area?
answer: Vegetables and rent have become costlier.

en: I have applied for a home loan.
tamil: நான் வீட்டுக் கடனுக்கு விண்ணப்பிச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Sharing news with a colleague.
explain: 'Have applied' shows you did it and are now waiting.
usage: Use it when you share a big money plan with friends or colleagues.
leelaQ: What kind of house would you like to buy?
answer: I would like a small house near my office.

en: You may get a better rate at another bank.
tamil: வேற வங்கியில இன்னும் நல்ல வட்டி கிடைக்கலாம்.
context: Giving advice to a friend about a deposit.
explain: 'May' shows a possibility, not a sure thing.
usage: Use it to suggest a friend compare banks before deciding.
leelaQ: How do you choose a bank?
answer: I check the interest rate and the nearest branch.

en: Does this bill include tax?
tamil: இந்த பில்ல வரி சேர்த்து இருக்கா?
context: Asking a cashier at a restaurant.
explain: 'Include' means the price already has the tax inside.
usage: Ask it at a restaurant or shop to understand the total price.
leelaQ: Do you read your bills before paying?
answer: Yes, I read them quickly before I pay.

en: I will ask my father before I sign anything.
tamil: எதுலயும் கையெழுத்து போடறதுக்கு முன்னாடி அப்பாகிட்ட கேட்பேன்.
context: Telling an agent you need advice first.
explain: 'Before I sign' uses the present tense after 'before' even for the future.
usage: Use it to politely slow down an agent who is in a hurry.
leelaQ: Who do you ask for advice about money?
answer: I ask my father and my elder brother.

en: Could you send me your UPI ID?
tamil: உங்க UPI ஐடி அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend for payment details.
explain: 'Could you send me ...?' is polite and short.
usage: Use it when you need to pay a friend or a seller by phone.
leelaQ: What do you need to send money to someone?
answer: I need their phone number or UPI ID.

en: My brother lent me two thousand rupees.
tamil: என் அண்ணன் எனக்கு ரெண்டாயிரம் ரூபாய் கடன் கொடுத்தார்.
context: Telling a friend how you managed a payment.
explain: 'Lent' is the past of 'lend'. Borrow and lend are opposites.
usage: Use it when you explain where you got money from.
leelaQ: Did anyone help you with money when you needed it?
answer: Yes, my brother helped me once.

en: How do I reset my net banking password?
tamil: என் நெட் பேங்கிங் பாஸ்வேர்டை எப்படி மாத்தறது?
context: Asking a bank helpdesk.
explain: 'How do I ...?' asks for the way to do something.
usage: Ask it at the bank or on a helpline when you cannot log in.
leelaQ: How do you remember all your passwords?
answer: I write hints in a safe notebook.

en: Rent takes almost half of my salary.
tamil: வாடகை என் சம்பளத்துல கிட்டத்தட்ட பாதி எடுத்துக்குது.
context: Talking about living costs in a big city.
explain: 'Takes half of my salary' means half of the money goes there.
usage: Use it when you talk about the cost of living.
leelaQ: How much of your income goes on housing?
answer: About one third of my income goes on housing.

en: I did not know about the hidden charges.
tamil: மறைமுக கட்டணங்கள் பத்தி எனக்கு தெரியாது.
context: Complaining to a service provider.
explain: 'Hidden charges' are costs nobody told you about.
usage: Use it when you complain about a surprise fee on a bill.
leelaQ: What should you do when you see a strange charge?
answer: I should ask the company to explain it.

en: She is paying the school fees at the counter.
tamil: அவங்க கவுண்டர்ல பள்ளிக் கட்டணம் கட்டிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Telling someone where your wife is.
explain: Present continuous with 'is' describes something happening now.
usage: Use it when you explain where someone is right now.
leelaQ: How do parents usually pay school fees?
answer: They pay online or at the school office.

en: Please call me when the money comes.
tamil: பணம் வந்ததும் எனக்கு கூப்பிடுங்க.
context: Asking a friend to inform you.
explain: 'When' with the present tense talks about a future time.
usage: Use it when you wait for a payment and need a quick update.
leelaQ: Who do you call first when you get good news?
answer: I call my mother first.

en: The bank manager explained the loan process to us.
tamil: வங்கி மேலாளர் லோன் நடைமுறையை எங்களுக்கு விளக்கினார்.
context: Telling a friend about a bank visit.
explain: 'Explained ... to us' shows who got the explanation.
usage: Use it when you talk about a visit to the bank.
leelaQ: Have you ever met a bank manager? What did you ask?
answer: Yes, I asked about a savings scheme.

en: Will you pay by cash or by card?
tamil: ரொக்கமா கட்டுவீங்களா, கார்டா?
context: A cashier asking a customer.
explain: 'Or' gives two choices. 'By cash' and 'by card' show the method.
usage: A shop cashier asks this at the counter when billing.
leelaQ: Which is safer, cash or card?
answer: Cards are safer because we can block them if lost.

en: Online shopping often gives good cashback offers.
tamil: ஆன்லைன் ஷாப்பிங்ல அடிக்கடி நல்ல கேஷ்பேக் ஆஃபர் கிடைக்கும்.
context: Telling a friend about a saving tip.
explain: 'Often' shows how frequently something happens.
usage: Use it in chats about saving money while shopping.
leelaQ: Do you buy things online? What was your last order?
answer: Yes, my last order was a pair of shoes.

en: The price has gone up since last week.
tamil: போன வாரத்துல இருந்து விலை ஏறிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a customer about a price change.
explain: 'Since' is used with present perfect for a starting point in time.
usage: Use it when you notice prices change in shops or online.
leelaQ: Which thing became expensive recently?
answer: Tomatoes became expensive recently.

en: Could you tell me where the closest cash machine is?
tamil: பக்கத்துல கேஷ் மெஷின் எங்க இருக்குன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a passer-by for directions to a cash machine.
explain: "Could you tell me" is polite, so the verb "is" comes after the place word.
usage: Ask it from a stranger or shopkeeper when you need cash quickly.
leelaQ: How do you find places when you are in a new city?
answer: I use a map app on my phone.

en: We should compare prices before we buy.
tamil: வாங்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி விலைகளை ஒப்பிட்டு பார்க்கணும்.
context: Advising your sister before shopping.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. 'Compare' means look at two or more things together.
usage: Use it when you give shopping advice to family.
leelaQ: How do you decide what to buy when two things look the same?
answer: I choose the one with the better price and quality.

en: I will not buy it unless the price comes down.
tamil: விலை குறையலனா நான் இதை வாங்க மாட்டேன்.
context: Telling a seller your limit.
explain: 'Unless' means 'if not'. 'Will not' is a firm decision.
usage: Use it while bargaining at a market or shop.
leelaQ: Do you bargain in shops? Why or why not?
answer: Yes, I bargain because small shops allow it.

en: I transferred the rent to the landlord this morning.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு காலையில வீட்டு உரிமையாளருக்கு வாடகை அனுப்பிட்டேன்.
context: Telling your flatmate the rent is done.
explain: 'This morning' with past tense is used when the morning is over.
usage: Use it with a flatmate or family member to confirm rent payment.
leelaQ: Do you rent a house or live in your own house?
answer: I live in my own house.

en: Is the interest rate fixed or floating?
tamil: வட்டி விகிதம் நிலையானதா, மாறக்கூடியதா?
context: Asking a loan officer.
explain: 'Fixed' means it does not change. 'Floating' means it can change.
usage: Ask it before you sign any loan paper.
leelaQ: Why do some people like a fixed rate?
answer: They like it because the payment stays the same.

en: May I see your ID proof, please?
tamil: உங்க அடையாள அட்டையை பார்க்கலாமா?
context: A bank staff member asking a customer.
explain: 'May I ...?' is a formal, polite request used in offices.
usage: Bank and office staff say this before they process a request.
leelaQ: What ID proofs do you carry with you?
answer: I carry my Aadhaar card and driving licence.

en: Many people in my village use UPI for small payments.
tamil: எங்க ஊர்ல நிறைய பேர் சின்ன பேமெண்டுக்கு UPI பயன்படுத்தறாங்க.
context: Telling a friend about digital payment use.
explain: 'Many people' takes a plural verb: use, not uses.
usage: Use it when you talk about how people pay in your area.
leelaQ: How has UPI changed life in small towns?
answer: Now even tea shops take payments on the phone.

en: If I save every month, I will buy a laptop soon.
tamil: ஒவ்வொரு மாசமும் சேமிச்சா சீக்கிரம் லேப்டாப் வாங்கிடுவேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a goal.
explain: 'If' + present, then 'will' shows a real possibility.
usage: Use it when you talk about a goal you are saving for.
leelaQ: What are you saving money for?
answer: I am saving money for a laptop.

en: I don't use credit cards because I spend too much.
tamil: நான் அதிகமா செலவு பண்ணுவேன்னு கிரெடிட் கார்டு பயன்படுத்தறதில்ல.
context: Explaining your money habit.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Don't use' is the negative present.
usage: Use it when someone asks why you do not have a credit card.
leelaQ: Do you spend more when you shop online?
answer: Yes, I sometimes buy things I do not need.

en: How much did you pay for this?
tamil: இதுக்கு நீங்க எவ்வளவு கொடுத்தீங்க?
context: Asking a friend about a new thing.
explain: 'How much did you pay' asks the price of something bought.
usage: Ask it with friends when you admire something new they bought.
leelaQ: What was the last thing you bought and how much was it?
answer: I bought a bag and it cost five hundred rupees.

en: The bank is giving a good rate on fixed deposits.
tamil: வங்கி ஃபிக்ஸட் டெபாசிட்டுக்கு நல்ல வட்டி தருது.
context: Telling your uncle about an offer.
explain: Present continuous shows an offer that is available now.
usage: Use it with family when you share news about a savings offer.
leelaQ: What do older people in your family do with their savings?
answer: They keep it in fixed deposits.

en: Wait here while I withdraw some cash.
tamil: நான் கொஞ்சம் பணம் எடுக்கற வரை இங்க இருங்க.
context: Asking a friend to wait outside an ATM.
explain: 'While' connects two actions at the same time.
usage: Say it to a friend or driver when you go to an ATM.
leelaQ: Do you feel safe using an ATM at night?
answer: No, I prefer to go in the daytime.

en: My account got blocked after three wrong PIN attempts.
tamil: மூணு தடவை தப்பான பின் போட்டதுனால என் கணக்கு பிளாக் ஆயிடுச்சு.
context: Reporting a problem at the bank.
explain: 'Got blocked' is a common spoken passive form.
usage: Use it at the bank or on a helpline when a card or account stops working.
leelaQ: What would you do if your account is blocked?
answer: I would go to the bank with my ID.

en: We have cleared all our credit card dues.
tamil: எங்க கிரெடிட் கார்டு பாக்கி எல்லாம் அடைச்சிட்டோம்.
context: Sharing good news with a friend.
explain: 'Have cleared' shows the work is complete now.
usage: Use it when you tell friends or family you are free of debt.
leelaQ: How does it feel when you finish paying a loan?
answer: It feels like a big weight is gone.

en: Can I pay the school fee in instalments?
tamil: பள்ளிக் கட்டணத்தை தவணையில கட்டலாமா?
context: Asking the school office.
explain: 'In instalments' means in smaller parts over time.
usage: Ask it at a school or college office when the full fee is hard to pay.
leelaQ: Why do people like paying in instalments?
answer: Because it is easier to pay small amounts.

en: A good budget helps you avoid debt.
tamil: நல்ல பட்ஜெட் கடன் வராம தவிர்க்க உதவும்.
context: Giving a friend money advice.
explain: 'Helps you avoid' is a useful pattern: help + person + verb.
usage: Use it when you give simple money advice to younger people.
leelaQ: What is one tip you can give a new college student about money?
answer: Write down every expense and spend carefully.

en: You can check your balance on the mobile app.
tamil: மொபைல் ஆப்ல உங்க இருப்பை பார்க்கலாம்.
context: Helping an elderly person with banking.
explain: 'Can' shows that something is possible.
usage: Use it when you teach an elder a simple banking step.
leelaQ: Have you taught anyone to use a banking app?
answer: Yes, I taught my mother to use it.

en: Gold is not cheap anymore.
tamil: தங்கம் இப்போ மலிவு இல்ல.
context: Talking about jewellery prices.
explain: 'Not ... anymore' shows something was true before but is not true now.
usage: Use it when you talk about prices with family before a purchase.
leelaQ: What was cheap in the past but is costly now?
answer: Tea and bus tickets were cheap in the past.

en: Why is the electricity bill so high this month?
tamil: இந்த மாசம் கரண்ட் பில் ஏன் இவ்வளவு அதிகம்?
context: Asking your family at home.
explain: 'So high' stresses that the amount is surprising.
usage: Use it at home, or with the electricity office, when a bill looks wrong.
leelaQ: How can a family reduce its electricity use?
answer: We can switch off fans and lights when we leave a room.

en: He paid the vegetable seller by scanning a QR code.
tamil: அவர் QR கோடை ஸ்கேன் பண்ணி காய்கறிக்காரருக்கு பணம் கொடுத்தார்.
context: Describing how people pay in a market.
explain: 'By scanning' shows the way something was done.
usage: Use it when you tell a story about digital payments in daily life.
leelaQ: Do vegetable sellers near you accept phone payments?
answer: Yes, many of them have a QR code board.

en: Could you lower the interest a little?
tamil: வட்டியை கொஞ்சம் குறைக்க முடியுமா?
context: Negotiating with a loan agent.
explain: 'A little' makes the request softer and more polite.
usage: Use it politely when you talk to a loan agent or a lender.
leelaQ: Do you think it is okay to negotiate with a bank?
answer: Yes, it is okay to ask for a better rate.

en: I'll check my bank statement tonight.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி என் வங்கி அறிக்கையை பார்ப்பேன்.
context: Promising to look into a payment.
explain: 'I'll' is the short form of 'I will'. It is common in speech.
usage: Say it when someone asks about a payment you need to verify.
leelaQ: How often do you go through your bank statement?
answer: I go through it once a month.

en: My mother keeps a small savings box at home.
tamil: என் அம்மா வீட்டுல ஒரு சின்ன உண்டியல் வச்சிருக்காங்க.
context: Telling a friend about a family habit.
explain: Simple present with 'keeps' shows a regular habit.
usage: Use it when you talk about saving habits in your family.
leelaQ: Did you save coins in a box when you were a child?
answer: Yes, I saved coins in a small box.

en: I can't afford a new phone right now.
tamil: இப்போ புது போன் வாங்க என்னால முடியாது.
context: Explaining to a friend why you will not buy.
explain: 'Can't afford' means you do not have enough money for something.
usage: Use it honestly with friends or sellers when something is beyond your budget.
leelaQ: What would you like to buy if money was not a problem?
answer: I would buy a new phone and a laptop.

en: Is the bank open on the second Saturday of the month?
tamil: மாசத்தோட இரண்டாவது சனிக்கிழமை வங்கி திறந்திருக்குமா?
context: Asking a bank clerk about weekend working days.
explain: Many banks in India are closed on the second Saturday, so people check first.
usage: Ask it at the bank gate or on a helpline to plan your visit.
leelaQ: When do you find time to visit the bank?
answer: I go on Saturday mornings.

en: I have set a monthly limit for my spending.
tamil: என் செலவுக்கு ஒரு மாசாந்திர வரம்பு வச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend about your money control.
explain: 'Have set' shows a rule you made that still applies.
usage: Use it when you discuss money habits with friends.
leelaQ: How do you control your spending?
answer: I set a limit and track it in a notebook.

en: Prices are rising, so we are cutting small expenses.
tamil: விலை ஏறிட்டே போகுது, அதனால சின்ன செலவுகளை குறைக்கிறோம்.
context: Explaining a family decision.
explain: 'So' connects a cause and its result.
usage: Use it when you explain why a family is spending less.
leelaQ: Which small expenses can you cut easily?
answer: I can cut eating outside and online orders.

en: I paid the full amount and got a discount.
tamil: நான் முழு தொகையை கட்டினேன், தள்ளுபடி கிடைச்சுது.
context: Telling a friend about a good deal.
explain: Two past actions joined by 'and'.
usage: Use it when you share a money-saving experience.
leelaQ: Have you ever got a discount for paying early?
answer: Yes, I got a small discount on my insurance.
